## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Double-anonymous: the publish-with-us page says editors will guide manuscripts "through the double-anonymized peer review process" (copy 2026-02-10), and the guidelines say authors' identities are not shown to reviewers and reviewers do not identify themselves; author names, institutional information and any author information in an OSF preregistration are to be removed, and own work cited in normal citation style, not as "Authors" and not with self-referential wording (guidelines copy 2026-02-15, https://web.archive.org/web/20260215021251/https://academic.oup.com/jcmc/pages/General_Instructions) |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Blank. No transfer statement found in the guidelines copy |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | Blank. No statement found in the guidelines copy |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | Blank. No source (SciRev has no reviews). The guidelines treat revisions and resubmissions as subject to the same 10,000-word limit (guidelines copy 2026-02-15) |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Authors are welcome to suggest reviewer names in the cover letter (guidelines copy 2026-02-15). Decision wording is not published |

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | Yes, by reference. The guidelines say authors should review the ICA Publications Committee's guidelines for generative AI for all ICA publications and that, in the cover letter, authors should disclose any use of AI in the research process, including writing, proofreading, data collection or other activities; some uses must also appear in the Methods or another section (guidelines copy 2026-02-15). The ICA recommendation itself (undated one-page PDF, retrieved 2026-11-23) says AI software should not be listed as an author, that use of AI-generated content or analysis in the research workflow must be noted in the Methods (or Acknowledgments) at submission, and that editors and reviewers must disclose their own use; it adds that editorial decisions on AI use in submitted manuscripts are made by each journal's editorial team |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | No gate found: use is allowed with disclosure |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 (allowed with mandatory disclosure; same rubric as other AI-researched entries) |
| **Summary** | Disclosure in the cover letter and, where the use belongs to the method, in the Methods; no AI authorship; no ban on use stated |
| **Source URL** | https://web.archive.org/web/20260215021251/https://academic.oup.com/jcmc/pages/General_Instructions (journal rule); https://cdn.ymaws.com/www.icahdq.org/resource/resmgr/docs/AI_Pub_Comm_Recomendations.pdf (ICA recommendation) |

### Preprint Policy

> Journal sentence plus the publisher's self-archiving policy. Sources: guidelines copy 2026-02-15 and https://web.archive.org/web/20261102215712/https://academic.oup.com/pages/self_archiving_policy_b (OUP author self-archiving policy, snapshot 2026-11-02).

| Stage | Allowed? | Notes |
|-------|----------|-------|
| Pre-submission | Yes | The guidelines say authors keep the right to make an Author's Original Version available through various channels and that this does not prevent submission. The OUP policy lets authors post it anywhere at any time, provided that, once accepted, they add a short acknowledgment that it was accepted by the journal |
| Under review | Not separately stated | Neither the guidelines nor the OUP policy address the under-review stage on its own. Anonymous review depends on authors not exposing identity (see Peer Review) |
| Post-acceptance (AAM) | Not needed | The journal is fully open access (see Open Access), so the accepted article is published under an open licence; the OUP accepted-manuscript embargo list applies to subscription titles and was not read for this journal |
| Version of Record | Open licence | The guidelines list a "CC BY licence - $0" line and say all accepted articles are published under an open access licence on publication (guidelines copy 2026-02-15) |

## Format

> Source for the rules below: the guidelines page, Wayback copy dated 2026-02-15 (https://web.archive.org/web/20260215021251/https://academic.oup.com/jcmc/pages/General_Instructions). The live page may differ.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Original research articles and meta-analyses of prior research (about copy 2026-02-08 and call-for-papers copy 2024-05-29). OpenAlex type counts for 2021-01-01 to 2026-11-23: 187 articles, 8 errata, 1 editorial, 1 retraction, 1 review (retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Word limit** | All manuscripts, including revisions and resubmissions, under 10,000 words including the abstract, references, tables, figures, appendices and endnotes; authors with "special circumstances" are told to email the editor-in-chief (guidelines copy 2026-02-15) |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Stated route to an exception: the guidelines invite authors to email the editor-in-chief if special circumstances warrant a longer submission. No figure on how often this is granted |
| **Abstract limit** | Maximum 250 words and 5-7 keywords on page 1; a lay summary of at most 200 words is requested after acceptance (guidelines copy 2026-02-15) |
| **Reference limit** | No separate cap; references count inside the 10,000 words. APA 7th edition; references start on a new page; DOIs are included in https://doi.org/ form |
| **Supplementary material** | Supplemental materials are allowed and not counted in the word total; material the main manuscript refers to (for example appendices) must be uploaded at submission; online supplements may be PDFs (guidelines copy 2026-02-15) |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit found. Tables, figures, appendices and endnotes go after the references; alt text for each figure is required, placed under the figure legend and preceded by "Alt text:" (guidelines copy 2026-02-15) |
| **Style / submission format** | APA 7th edition; headings in title case, at most 5 levels; 12-point Times New Roman, double-spaced, 1.0 inch margins; a single Word main document ("We do not accept PDF files"); submitted through the journal's ScholarOne site; submissions that do not follow APA 7th or the stated rules may be returned without review (guidelines copy 2026-02-15) |

### Orientation

> Counts below come from Crossref journal-article records for 2021-01 to 2026-11-23: 200 records, of which 191 (95.5%) carry an abstract; a record is counted when the pattern matches in its title or abstract; shares use the 191 as the denominator (https://api.crossref.org/journals/1083-6101/works, cursor paging, retrieved 2026-11-23). Every regex is given in Methodological Preferences and Sensitive Topics. The first-pass tool `topic_trend_scan.py` was not used (known broken).

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Empirical vs. Theoretical** | Empirical designs dominate by keyword: experiment-type words in 43 of 191 abstracts (22.5%), survey-type words in 37 (19.4%); a broad conceptual/theoretical pattern matches 26 (13.6%), but it also matches empirical abstracts that name a theory, so it is not a count of purely theoretical papers. The journal's own text asks for work that is "theoretically grounded" (call-for-papers copy 2024-05-29) |
| **Quantitative vs. Qualitative** | Quantitative designs are more frequent; interview-type words appear in 33 (17.3%) and qualitative-method words in 24 (12.6%) of 191 abstracts |
| **Cross-disciplinary openness** | Stated: the journal is "broadly interdisciplinary", publishing scholars of communication, business, education, political science, sociology, psychology, media studies and information science (about copy 2026-02-08, https://web.archive.org/web/20260208082331/https://academic.oup.com/jcmc/pages/About). The editor writes that there is "no requirement to be limited to communication theories" (call-for-papers copy 2024-05-29, https://web.archive.org/web/20240529201158/https://academic.oup.com/jcmc/pages/call-for-papers) |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** One scope condition is stated: the focus is "social science research on communicating using computer-based media technologies" (call-for-papers copy 2024-05-29, https://web.archive.org/web/20240529201158/https://academic.oup.com/jcmc/pages/call-for-papers); the about-page copy of 2026-02-08 words the same focus as communicating "with" computer-based media technologies (https://web.archive.org/web/20260208082331/https://academic.oup.com/jcmc/pages/About).
- **What kind of engagement?** The editor describes the "canonical" paper as theoretically grounded yet innovative, powered by diverse datasets, methods and disciplinary traditions, and clearly written; she says the core questions are those central to communication but there is no requirement to use communication theories, and she wants more "big ideas" scholarship alongside work that furthers technology-relevant theory (call-for-papers copy 2024-05-29, https://web.archive.org/web/20240529201158/https://academic.oup.com/jcmc/pages/call-for-papers).
- **Article type and length**: original research articles and meta-analyses; under 10,000 words including references; abstract up to 250 words; 5-7 keywords; a lay summary after acceptance (guidelines copy 2026-02-15, https://web.archive.org/web/20260215021251/https://academic.oup.com/jcmc/pages/General_Instructions).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: manuscripts that do not follow APA 7th or the stated requirements, or that are "otherwise deemed unsuitable", are returned to authors without review (guidelines copy 2026-02-15). A contact-the-editors page routes "submission fit and scope" questions to a named editor (copy 2026-02-14, https://web.archive.org/web/20260214041520/https://academic.oup.com/jcmc/pages/contact-the-editors). No data on out-of-scope rejections exists (SciRev: no reviews).

### Methodological Preferences

> Counts: Crossref journal-article records 2021-01 to 2026-11-23, 200 records, 191 with an abstract; a hit is a match in title or abstract; share = hits / 191. Scoring convention of this research pass (its own, not an external standard): share 0 = 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement. The editor's statements (diverse datasets and methods; meta-analyses listed as an acceptable format) welcome methods in general but favour none, so no row is scored 4 or 5. Scores measure how often a method appears, not how reviewers judge it. All patterns are case-insensitive Python regexes; in table cells the alternation bar is written `\|`, read as `|`.

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 3 | `\b(experiment\w*\|randomi[sz]ed\|between-subjects?\|within-subjects?)\b` 43 of 191 (22.5%); title-only 3 of 200. Survey pattern `\b(surveys?\|questionnaires?\|self-report\w*\|panel (?:survey\|data\|study))\b` 37 (19.4%). Preregistration pattern `\bpre-?regist\w*` 15 (7.9%); the guidelines ask authors to check that OSF preregistrations carry no author information (guidelines copy 2026-02-15) |
| Qualitative interviews | 3 | `\b(interview\w*\|semi-structured\|focus groups?)\b` 33 of 191 (17.3%); broader qualitative pattern `\b(qualitative\|thematic analysis\|ethnograph\w*\|discourse analysis\|grounded theory)\b` 24 (12.6%); title-only 2 of 200 |
| Autoethnography | 0 | `\bautoethnograph\w*` 0 of 191 abstracts and 0 titles |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 3 | `\b(conceptual\w*\|theori[sz]\w*)\b` 26 of 191 (13.6%); the pattern also matches empirical abstracts that mention a theory, so it overstates purely theoretical work; title-only 3 of 200 |
| Mixed methods | 2 | `\bmixed[- ]methods?\b` 4 of 191 (2.1%) |
| Meta-analysis / systematic review | 2 | `\b(meta-analy\w*\|systematic review\w*\|meta-synthesis\|scoping review)\b` 5 of 191 (2.6%); title-only 5 of 200 (e.g. https://doi.org/10.1093/jcmc/zmad055). The about page names meta-analyses of prior research as an acceptable format (about copy 2026-02-08), which is a statement of acceptance, not of preference; the score follows the count |
| Computational / digital-trace methods (added row) | 2 | `\b(computational\|machine learning\|topic model\w*\|natural language processing\|large language models?\|web tracking\|digital trace\w*)\b` 8 of 191 (4.2%); content-analysis pattern `\bcontent analys[ie]s\b` 3 (1.6%) |

### Voice & Style

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **First-person voice acceptance (0-5)** | Not scored. Sample (abstract-only text; titles and full texts not searched): in Crossref abstracts, 128 of 191 (67.0%) contain a first-person word (pattern `\b(?:I\|[Ww]e\|[Mm]y\|[Oo]ur)\b`, case-sensitive; plural "we" may be generic or authorial); among the 10 most recent abstracts by publication date, 6 contain one (DOIs ending zmag024, zmag019, zmag020, zmag022, zmag012, zmag014 contain it; zmag025, zmag016, zmag021, zmag023 do not; all under https://doi.org/10.1093/jcmc/). Abstracts only: full texts were not read; the guidelines give no first-person rule except that self-citations must not use "our"-style wording that reveals identity |
| **Expected density** | Length ceiling 10,000 words including references and endnotes (guidelines copy 2026-02-15). Crossref author lists for 192 of 200 records: 1 author 27, 2 authors 67, 3 authors 47, 4 or more 51 |
| **Abstract and keywords** | Maximum 250 words; 5-7 keywords; abstract on page 1; lay summary up to 200 words after acceptance, avoiding citations and abbreviations, with a Flesch Reading Ease above 65 recommended (guidelines copy 2026-02-15) |
| **Writing style notes** | APA 7th edition; headings in title case; alt text required for figures; own work cited in normal citation style, with no "Authors" placeholder (guidelines copy 2026-02-15, https://web.archive.org/web/20260215021251/https://academic.oup.com/jcmc/pages/General_Instructions). The editor asks for "clear and compelling writing" (call-for-papers copy 2024-05-29) |
| **Authorship pattern** | See the Crossref author-count line above; 27 of 192 records with author lists have one author (14%) |

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | No ethics-approval or consent rule found: the guidelines copy of 2026-02-15 has a Publication Ethics section (COPE standards; falsification, fabrication, plagiarism and duplicate publication unacceptable; screening with iThenticate and third-party tools for image alteration and paper mills) and no wording on institutional review, informed consent or human subjects (searched the page text for IRB, institutional review, informed consent, human subject: none) (https://web.archive.org/web/20260215021251/https://academic.oup.com/jcmc/pages/General_Instructions) |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author items exist but are a minority: 27 of 192 Crossref records with author lists (2021-2026) have one author; 67 have two and 98 have three or more |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | No rule found: the guidelines copy asks for removal of institutional information for review and mentions no affiliation requirement. The publish-with-us page says ICA members "can submit an unlimited number of papers" (copy 2026-02-10, https://web.archive.org/web/20260210124020/https://academic.oup.com/jcmc/pages/publish-with-us), a membership benefit whose scope was not read further |
| **Data transparency requirement** | A Data Availability Statement is a requirement for all manuscripts, under the heading "Data availability"; the journal "strongly encourages" making data available where ethically feasible; datasets must be cited with a persistent identifier; voluntary Open Science Badges (open materials, open data, preregistered) are offered after acceptance (guidelines copy 2026-02-15, https://web.archive.org/web/20260215021251/https://academic.oup.com/jcmc/pages/General_Instructions) |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Double-anonymous review: author names and institutional information removed, OSF preregistration checked for author information, self-citations in normal citation style (guidelines copy 2026-02-15, https://web.archive.org/web/20260215021251/https://academic.oup.com/jcmc/pages/General_Instructions). An Author's Original Version may be posted anywhere before acceptance (OUP policy copy 2026-11-02, https://web.archive.org/web/20261102215712/https://academic.oup.com/pages/self_archiving_policy_b), which would expose identity; whether the journal treats a posted preprint as a problem for anonymity is not stated |
| **AI use** | Disclosure in the cover letter, and in the Methods where the use belongs to the method; AI cannot be an author (ICA recommendation, https://cdn.ymaws.com/www.icahdq.org/resource/resmgr/docs/AI_Pub_Comm_Recomendations.pdf; guidelines copy 2026-02-15) |
| **Open access and cost** | Fully open access; APC currently waived (about copy 2026-02-08, https://web.archive.org/web/20260208082331/https://academic.oup.com/jcmc/pages/About); 198 of 198 OpenAlex works in the window are diamond open access |
| **Originality screening** | Manuscripts may be screened with iThenticate and, for image alteration and paper-mill activity, with third-party services; a manuscript not yet screened may be put through iThenticate before final acceptance (guidelines copy 2026-02-15, https://web.archive.org/web/20260215021251/https://academic.oup.com/jcmc/pages/General_Instructions) |

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Length**: manuscripts, revisions included, must be under 10,000 words including abstract, references, tables, figures, appendices and endnotes; the guidelines give an email route to the editor-in-chief for special circumstances (Format; guidelines copy 2026-02-15).
- **Anonymisation and format**: double-anonymous review with identifying information removed, and a Word file only (Peer Review, Format). The guidelines say manuscripts that do not follow APA 7th or the stated requirements may be returned without review.
- **Data availability statement**: required for all manuscripts (Practical Concerns), so a paper with no statable position on data access does not meet the rule.
- **AI disclosure**: use of AI anywhere in the research process must be disclosed in the cover letter (AI Policy); undisclosed use breaches the stated rule.
- No other hard blocker is supported by a fact read; ethics-approval rules are not on the page read (Practical Concerns).

### Soft Tax

- **Time**: no turnaround figure is published or reported by SciRev (Review Cycle Time), so planning cannot rest on a number.
- **Open access cost**: the APC is currently waived (Open Access); the page does not say whether that will change, so the cost for a future submission is unknown.
- **Reporting burden**: a data availability statement, alt text for every figure, a 200-word lay summary after acceptance, and open-science badge information are requested (Format, Practical Concerns).
- **Preprint and anonymity**: posting a preprint is allowed by the publisher but would expose identity under double-anonymous review (Preprint Policy, OPSEC compatibility).

### Best Suited For

- Experiments, surveys and interview studies about communication through digital media: experiment-type words in 43 of 191 abstracts, survey 37, interview 33 (Methodological Preferences).
- Work that crosses disciplines, which the journal states it wants (Orientation, Framing Requirements).
- Topics with regular coverage: social media (71 of 191), AI and algorithms (38), relationships (41, 21.5%, pattern `\b(relationships?\|friendship\w*\|romantic\|dating)\b`), well-being and mental health (31), privacy (21) (Epistemological & Political Leanings, Sensitive Topics).
- Authors able to cover a long manuscript in 10,000 words and willing to share data or materials (Format, Practical Concerns).

### Not Recommended For

- Autoethnography: 0 of 191 abstracts and 0 titles match (Methodological Preferences). This shows absence, not rejection.
- Authors needing a verified turnaround or acceptance figure: the journal publishes none and SciRev has no reviews (Review Cycle Time, Metrics).
- Work with no connection to computer-based media, since the stated focus is social science research on communicating with computer-based media technologies (Framing Requirements).
- Authors who rely on the waived fee staying waived: the page says "currently" (Open Access).
